question: In recent years, and especially after the economic and geopolitical developments that followed Brexit, scenarios and political positions regarding the possible reintegration of the United Kingdom into the European Union have increasingly returned to the public debate.

Opinion polls, interventions by politicians and public interventions by representatives of civil society are recording increased interest in a rapprochement between London and Brussels. Brexit was an unprecedented political and institutional development for the European Union, with significant consequences for both the United Kingdom and the Member States.
At the same time, the need to strengthen European cooperation in areas such as defence, education, the economy and energy makes the relevant debate particularly timely. Accordingly: 1.
How does the Commission assess the public debates and political positions on the possible re-integration of the United Kingdom into the European Union?
In the event of a future request for re-integration, what procedure would be provided for institutionally and under what fundamental conditions?
answer: EN on behalf of the European Commission (20.7.2026) 1. The Commission does not comment on domestic debates in third countries. The choice to apply to become a member of the EU is entirely a prerogative of the United Kingdom. 2. Article 49 of the Treaty on European Union defines the procedure for a third country to become a member of the EU. As a first step, this country must address its application to the Council.

Under the same Article of the Treaty on European Union, the application is notified to national parliaments and the European Parliament. The Council decides on the application by unanimity, after receiving consent from the European Parliament by the majority of its members, on the basis of an opinion of the Commission on the readiness of the applicant country to become a member.

All Member States need to sign and ratify the accession treaty which enables the country to become a member of the EU. This treaty may include conditions of admission and adjustments to the Treaties on which the EU is founded.
